note: Shared comparison cases for the two engines that must agree on what counts as the same soldier name: the game client (IronPath/character-name.mjs, policy NFC_CASEFOLD_V2) and the offline audit script (IronPath/scripts/audit-character-names.py, Unicode default case folding). Both engines now agree on every case: `same` and `casefoldSame` match across the board, including expanding sharp s (`Straße` == `STRASSE`), final sigma (`ΜΑΡΚΟΣ` == `μαρκοσ`), and typographic ligatures (`ﬁn` == `FIN`). Changing either engine without updating this file causes both test suites to fail.

cases.why: outer ECMAScript whitespace is not a difference
composed and decomposed accents normalize to the same form
non-Latin case is still not a difference
UNIFIED STRICT CASEFOLD (NFC_CASEFOLD_V2): Unicode default case folding expands ß and ẞ to ss in both client and audit
accented vs unaccented letters remain distinct in both engines
Greek medial and final sigma fold identically under Unicode default case folding
Unicode default case folding expands Latin typographic ligatures identically
compatibility fullwidth characters are not conflated by either engine; a stricter character rule would be a separate decision
trailing space in a stored legacy name is not a new name
